text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Crown Prince Hassan meets President Bill Clinton, says Jordan appreciates setting up of U.S. fund to support peace and stability in the Middle East and will not abandon its hopes and efforts for peace.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali assures Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat of Jordan's support in all forms to brotherly Palestinians.
- Killer of Syrian family in Amman arrested.
- Today is deadline for foreign workers in Jordan to get their papers in order.
- Jordan Valley authorities to start allocating on Saturday agricultural land irrigated by new extension of King Abdullah Canal.

- Planning Minister Rima Khalaf says not true that half of Jordan's extra $100 million aid from United States is actually being taken from U.S. aid to Israel. Khalaf says the money Jordan is getting is all American.
- Former Israeli Prime Minister Shimon Peres to deliver U.N. lecture on leadership in Amman tomorrow.

- Head of the board of Bank of Jordan, Tawfiq al-Fakhouri, says the bank to propose to shareholders in the next two weeks a meeting to discuss doubling capital to 21 million dinars ($30 million). Half the increase will be funded by open subscription of new shares; the other half by transfer of cash from reserves and retained profits, with bonus half-shares issued to existing shareholders.
- Crown Prince Hassan tells Clinton that Jordan rejects any changes to the map of the Middle East.
- Jordan's ambassador to Israel says Isarelis harassing Jordanian diplomats. Says one diplomat was nearly handcuffed during a security check.
- Chief Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat says Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu encourages settlers to confiscate more land.
